Authors report inconsistent extraction/reasoning from solver numbers for both vendors, even when sweeps were correctly implemented; no rate is tabulated.
Large-grid failures involved deep-copy/linear-lookup backend costs and oversized model context; source describes roughly quadratic sweep cost.
At L3, the OpenAI agent explored element/contingency definitions without sending a contingency to the solver; counts not tabulated.

interpretation_limits: The 12 searches are 4 backends × 3 applications on one grid, not 12 repetitions of one task and not a reliability estimate.
All 12 avoided fatal JSON parsing failures; that metric does not establish complete or correct engineering conclusions.
PFLOW cost reductions from unit commitment change the allowed action space; do not plot them as improvements for the requested dispatch-only task.
Convergence and feasibility concern the modeled cases and declared constraints; they do not certify full contingency coverage, correct reporting or operating authorization.
Do not merge R01's September prototype results with R02's July development-snapshot results into a model leaderboard.

illustrative_statistics.status: Mathematical teaching illustrations, not empirical results from the grid papers

zero_failure.formula: One-sided 95% upper bound on failure probability after 0 failures in n independent fixed-setting Bernoulli trials: 1−0.05^(1/n)
zero_failure.assumption: Independent identically distributed Bernoulli attempts with a fixed failure definition. Repeated agent tests may not satisfy these assumptions; this does not bound unknown operating conditions.

serial_steps.formula: P(all L steps correct)=q^L if each step succeeds independently with the same probability q
serial_steps.assumption: Illustrative independence and constant per-step probability; real agent errors can be correlated.
